newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-SELES STOPS COETZER TO REACH FINAL AGAINST HINGIS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SELES STOPS COETZER TO REACH FINAL AGAINST HINGIS.

text.p: Second seed Monica Seles hammered out a 6-3 6-4 victory over stubborn South African Amanda Coetzer Saturday to reach the final of the Toshiba Tennis Classic and a showdown with top-ranked Martina Hingis.

The 16-year-old Swiss sensation, who has been dominating the women's game as Seles did earlier in the decade, roared into her 10th final in as many tournaments earlier Saturday by destroying sixth seed Mary Pierce.
Hingis played a near flawless match and even unleashed seven aces for a 6-0 6-2 49-minute thumping of Pierce in a rematch of the Australian Open final.
"I played so good, I almost didn't make one error," said a delighted Hingis after moving within one win of her ninth title of the year.

Seles, who reached her fourth final but is still looking for her first title of the year, raised her game enough to take out the third-seeded Coetzer in straight sets. But she knows she will have to turn it up a lot higher Sunday.
"It was good tennis but not the calibre to win against Martina," Seles said. "If I make a lot of errors I have zero chances because she's so consistent."

With the top seed's gaudy 53-1 1997 match record and the Wimbledon and Australian Open titles under her belt, Seles has a pretty good idea where Hingis is mentally when she takes the court these days.
"Steffi (Graf) was in the zone, I was in the zone and now she's there," Seles said of Hingis.
"She's playing very confident and some some great tennis. She's got both things going for her and her record is unbelievable. I'm going to have to play some great tennis (to beat her).
"Maybe I can rise up to the occasion like some players do when they play me."
Seles captured the opening set from Coetzer with the help of a crucial service break in the eighth game.
The sixth-ranked South African had visions of forcing a third set after going up a break with a 3-1 lead in the second. But Seles dug down and ran off five of the last six games to end the contest.
"I tried to cut down on my errors. It was all up to me and I did that," said Seles, who is sure to make a better showing against Hingis than Pierce.

Pierce had been in such good form in her quarter-final win over French compatriot Sandrine Testud Friday that it seemed she might be able to give Hingis a contest. But that challenge never materialised with Pierce winning just eight points in the shockingly brief first set.
"This match to me wasn't a match," Pierce said.
"When you lose the first set 6-0 in 18 minutes, you know nothing happened. It was just mistake, next point."
But the next point wasn't much better for Pierce, who double-faulted away the opening game of the second set as the rout continued to its inevitable conclusion.
"Mary, she was trying but she played a very risky match," Hingis said, "and I played a great match."
